title: Why Medical AI Needs a Referee | Protege's Engy Ziedan
content: Medical AI faces a measurement problem: high benchmark scores do not guarantee real-world clinical readiness. Engy Ziedan of Protege argues for independent evaluations that assess actual workflow performance rather than static tests. Risks include subtle bias, prompt-dependent ranking variability, and misalignment between benchmarks and clinical needs. Contaminated training data can distort benchmarks. As AI becomes more personalized and evolves rapidly, continuous monitoring may be needed instead of periodic testing.

title: 折叠 iPhone 最全爆料汇总：用过的都说好，但有两个大缺点
content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone will be a book-style device with a 5.5-inch outer screen and 7.8-inch inner screen, featuring a nearly invisible crease and slim 4.5mm profile when unfolded. Early testers praised the pocketable size and hinge durability, while the expanded interface adopts an iPad-like layout powered by iOS 27's new adaptive design framework.

However, two major compromises stand out: no telephoto camera—only main and ultra-wide lenses—and the replacement of Face ID with side-mounted Touch ID to save internal space. Priced above $2,000, this niche debut product prioritizes foldable form factor over Pro-tier features, targeting wealthy early adopters rather than mass consumers, particularly in China, the world's largest foldable market.

content: Kweichow Moutai faces its first annual revenue and profit decline in over 20 years due to industry cyclical downturn, not business deterioration. Its core Feitian Moutai remains stable while series wine declines. The company is shifting from distributor-heavy to direct-to-consumer sales, now exceeding 50% of revenue, reclaiming pricing power and channel profits. Despite falling growth rates, Moutai maintains 91.2% gross margin, strong pricing control, and increased dividend payout ratio to 79%. Current PE of 20x represents a decade low, near 4% dividend yield. The analysis concludes Moutai is a quality business temporarily suppressed by cyclical headwinds rather than a value trap.

Corporate income tax, individual income tax, and import-related taxes all exceeded overall tax growth, with personal income tax surging 25.9%. Their wheeled dual-arm robots now serve ~500 Shanghai households for childcare, light chores, and pet care. title: 对阿里800亿港元配售的解读与思考
content:
Alibaba is raising HK$80 billion through its first Hong Kong share placement since 2019, the largest follow-on offering in HKEX history. The funds will fully fund AI infrastructure investment. The offering priced at 8.37% discount to last close, diluting existing shareholders by 3.80%, with no lock-up for institutional investors.

The move sparks controversy: critics note the amount roughly equals estimated losses from Alibaba's costly food delivery battle with Meitong, and contrast its direct, rapid-placement approach with Google's more diluted, staggered financing methods. Alibaba chose speed over shareholder smoothing due to high interest rates and competitive urgency.

Alibaba is not cash-poor—reserves exist—but free cash flow has been negative for five consecutive quarters amid surging capex (RMB67.7 billion last quarter, up 75% YoY). The company has already spent RMB190 billion of its three-year RMB380 billion AI investment
